newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Lebed says Russian troops to keep leaving Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: Lebed says Russian troops to keep leaving Chechnya.

text.p: Russian troop will continue with a planned withdrawal from Chechnya, security chief Alexander Lebed was quoted as saying on Tuesday after a meeting in the region with separatist leader Zelimkhan Yandarbiyev.

Itar-Tass news agency said Lebed told reporters that he and rebel leaders had confirmed their commitment to a peace deal they signed on August 31. The "demilitarisation" of the capital Grozny would also be continued, Lebed added.

Tass said the meeting, in the village of Novye Atagi, 20 km (12 miles) south of Grozny, had finished but gave no other details. Lebed's spokesman was earlier quoted as saying the Kremlin security chief would return to Moscow later in the day.

In the morning he had met General Vyacheslav Tikhomirov, the Russian army commander in the region. Last week Tikhomirov had suspended the withdrawal foreseen by the peace deal almost as soon as it began, citing a dispute over exchanging prisoners.
Lebed went to Chechnya after meeting Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and top officials at the weekend to map out Russia's position in future peace talks.
The former general has frequently criticised elements in Moscow and the army who he says have been obstructive in his attempts to reach a lasting peace settlement.
